question: Which organ meat should I feed as a treat for which part of my dog — and how much of each?
answer:
⚪ TCVM (traditional 'like supports like') + established nutrition — a quick organ-to-system treat guide: 

• HEART → supports the heart; rich in taurine, CoQ10, and B12. KEY POINT most people get wrong: heart is a MUSCLE, not a secreting organ, so it is NOT capped at 10% — you can feed it more freely as a treat or topper. 
• LIVER → supports the liver/detox; loaded with vitamin A, iron, B12, folate. It's the most nutrient-dense, so LIMIT it to about 5% of the diet (freeze-dried liver makes a great training treat, but count it toward that limit — too much causes vitamin A/copper overload). 
• KIDNEY → supports the kidneys; high in selenium, B12, vitamin A. Secreting organ, so count it in the organ allowance. 
• SPLEEN → supports blood/immune (TCVM); iron-rich. 
• PANCREAS → traditional digestive-enzyme support. 
• LUNG → traditional TCVM respiratory support. 
• GREEN TRIPE → not a 'like-feeds-like' organ but great for gut/digestion (natural enzymes + probiotics). 

DOSING RULE: secreting organs together (liver + kidney + spleen + pancreas) should be roughly 10–15% of the diet, with LIVER specifically ≤5%; heart and tripe sit outside that cap as muscle/gut foods. 

WHEN NOT to: introduce organs slowly (too much at once = loose stool), don't exceed the liver limit, and use quality/organic sources where you can — organs concentrate whatever the animal was exposed to. This is supportive food, not a treatment for diagnosed organ disease. (TCVM like-supports-like — traditional; organ nutrient content & 10% rule — established raw-feeding nutrition.)
source: TCVM 'like supports like' (traditional) + whole-prey/raw-feeding nutrition (10% organ rule)
